notes.title: Rapture Update - Version 1.3
notes.content:
The third regular update for Rapture has been released! This update is primarily focused on introducing new content. More specifically this patch contains two new events, a new character with a unique gimmick, party randomization and a few new unlockable relics - plus a few noteable bug fixes.

[u][b]New Event - Perfect Clear[/b][/u]
A new type of event that appears on all layers past the first one as long as no player deaths have occured in battle. This event will raise all your attributes by 1 and allows you to learn the Perfect Strike, an ability that always scales off your highest attribute.

[u][b]New Character - Tamamo, The Mimic[/b][/u]
An intelligent fox with a talent for mimicry, Tamamo learns moves by directly observing enemies. Her only ability is "Imitate" which allows Tamamo to learn the last ability used by the target enemy. Abilities that are taught this way are always available to Tamamo however she can only learn up to 6 abilities in total. Once per floor, you may encounter a special event that allows Tamamo to reset any number of abilities.

[u][b]New Event - Ability Reset[/b][/u]
A unique event that occurs once per floor as long as Tamamo is in the party. This event will allow her to reset any number of abilities that she picked up back to "Imitate" for free.

[u][b]New Feature - Randomize Party[/b][/u]
You can now click "Randomize" during Party Selection and a new party will be generated for you. The game will attempt to create a balanced party composition by default, picking one character from the following categories: Healing, Defensive, Attacking and Utility. 

[u][b]New Unlockable Relics[/b][/u]
Three new unlockable relics have been added to Rapture. 
[list]
[*] [b]Halo [+1 All Stats][/b] - [i]Whenever you receive a healing effect, raise one of your stats at random by 1 stage. [/i]
Unlocked by encountering 5 Torii events.
[*] [b]Harvester [+2 Special][/b] -[i] Whenever you use an ability against an non-elite enemy, deal extra damage equal to 1/6th of his current health. If the target has Fear then deal damage equal to 1/5th of his current health instead. [/i]
Unlocked by incapacitating 400 enemies in total.
[*] [b]Jack-o-Lantern [+1 Attack, +1 Special] [/b]- [i]At the start of your turn you have a 50% chance to apply Fear to a random enemy for 2 turns. [/i]
Unlocked by collecting 300 Relics in total.
[/list]

[u][b]Noteable Bug Fixes:[/b][/u]
Fixed an issue with two Relic unlocks that required kills not working.
Fixed an issue with the Inventory screen's health display.
Fixed an issue with certain sounds ignoring sound volume levels.

notes.title: Rapture Version 1.2
notes.content:
The second regular update for Rapture is scheduled to be released tonight! This update contains a bunch of bug fixes and a new way to enjoy Rapture - Difficulty Settings! 

[h2]Difficulty Settings
[/h2]
There are currently two different levels of Difficulty, Easy and Normal mode. Normal mode is the default difficulty level of Rapture and it is designed to provide a fair challenge. However it can also be very punishing especially for newer players.

Easy mode is designed to provide a shorter and more relaxed game session. The enemies scaling is toned down significantly and the elite encounters are 15% weaker. This is also an ideal difficulty setting for new players or for experimentation.

In the future, I'm planning to add a way to directly modify how your run is generated as well. That would mean modifying the amount of enemies, relics and events that spawn - changing how enemies scale per encounter and raising the difficulty of boss fights.


[h2]Demo and OST Release
[/h2]
Rapture now has a Demo available! If you've been on the fence about Rapture I suggest you give it a try. The demo will only let you go as far as the end of the first layer and you're limited to using 10 out of the 16 characters.

Furthermore, I'm releasing a free Official Soundtrack for Rapture with all four tracks composed by [url=https://twitter.com/leit_motive]Jesse Myers[/url]. You'll be able to download the OST for free within the next few days! If you enjoyed Rapture's soundtrack I suggest you check out his other works too!

notes.title: Dev Log #2 - Ability Design
notes.content:
Recently I've been working on revisiting combat mechanics and fine tuning their balance as the release day inches closer. For today's developer log I'm going to be talking about a crucial part of combat - character abilities.

[h1]An Introduction to Combat[/h1]
Your primary objective during a combat encounter is to incapacitate all enemies by lowering their Health to zero while making sure your party survives. Each party takes turns to act with each active character taking one action per turn. In Rapture, the player's party will always act first in combat giving you a chance to cause some serious damage before the enemies have time to react.

[h1]Character Abilities Explained[/h1]
Each character has six different abilities in combat plus one powerful Limit Break that can be used after the Limit Break Gauge is maxed out. These abilities are divided into five different categories based on their function:
[list]
[*] Physical Attacks
[*] Special Attacks
[*] Shield
[*] Healing
[*] Utility
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37503523/e32ddfadb629f3420a117bcd8e1801bc2bccf489.gif[/img]
Physical and Special attack abilities are primarily focused on dealing damage using the appropriate attribute - Attack for physical attack and Special for special attacks. They also tend to have secondary effects such as dealing increased damage to low health enemies, inflicting status effects, lowering a target's stats etc.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37503523/c528164105830190bccdeea2d74495a2d4232423.gif[/img]
Shield abilities provide temporary Shields that act as a buffer to your Health. They are a great source of damage negation since they can be applied before the enemy acts. However, unless the target has the status effect Persistence, Shields will expire at the start of your party's turn. Furthermore, certain abilities have effects that directly manipulate Shields such as instantly breaking all of the target's Shields or converting them into healing.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37503523/c26cd12549059fa0f568c47d569501265f3645f8.gif[/img]
Healing abilities can be used to restore health to your injured allies while also providing them with secondary beneficial effects, such as applying positive status effects or raising their attributes. Rarely, certain healing abilities can also be used to revive incapacitated party members, with a portion of their health. Be careful as the Corruption status effect will cause any healing received to be turned into damage instead, making it a great tool to prevent or punish healing abilities.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37503523/6682a4a158397a0f4fb94faa956f17d22ff1ca70.gif[/img]
Finally let's talk about Utility abilities, they provide little in terms of damage or healing but instead focus on secondary effects such as applying status effects, raising or lowering stats in combat. Appropriate use of Utility abilities is the key to overcoming the odds in Rapture as they can greatly enhance your party or cripple the opposition.


Once again I'd like to thank you for taking the time to read through this dev log - we've been working hard to prepare for release and you can expect the game to be released by the end of August. In the next developer log we'll be taking a more in depth look at some of the characters that you can add to your party in Rapture.

I'd like to remind you that you can contact me via Twitter or through Discord, you can find the links below:
Discord - https://discord.gg/UB54wAv
Twitter - https://twitter.com/GameRapture

notes.title: Dev Log #1 - Status Effect Indicators
notes.content:
Status effects play a crucial role in combat and appropriate use of status effects can be the deciding factor between easily emerging victorious from an encounter or barely scraping by with a sliver of your health left. For the past few days I've been working on adding visual indicators to when a status effect is impacting your character.

[h1]Status Effect Indicators[/h1]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37503523/abcc554d3d3bb84f53eb11910e7fb5be59a2a3f1.gif[/img]
Fatigue is a very impactful status effect that reduces your damage output. This can debilitate your offensive and in turn let the enemies get the upper hand on you, so it's best to watch out for it. As of the current version of Rapture when a character uses an ability while they are Fatigued there will be a clear visual indicator in the sweat drops animation being played while the character is acting.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37503523/d943b77bc19a16481e21683a419fea9399073672.gif[/img]
Taunt is a status effect that lets you redirect enemy single target attacks to yourself, making it extremely useful for characters that are naturally defensive and providing a certain amount of safety to your more fragile characters. Whenever Taunt successfully redirects an attack, the new status indicator will notify the player by playing the Taunt animation. This will provide clarity as to which attacks were successfully redirected away from your party members.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37503523/44553c3c000e3478d0b174276abffebb3c9cdde8.gif[/img]
Let's take a look at Charm, which causes enemies to fight for you. Whenever an enemy acts against their own party members while Charmed, a new visual indicator will clearly convey that information to the player.

Almost all status effects had visual indicators added to them, but you'll have to see the rest for yourself!


[h1]Side Note - Battle Victory Animations[/h1]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37503523/8d2241103fc014dea14809e84e2d34af2adb6544.gif[/img]
Finally, as a little side project this week I added walking animations to all characters, and they will now walk off stage (whenever possible) when successfully beating the encounter.

I'd like to thank you for taking the time to read through this dev log, I hope you found it interesting and there will be plenty more coming soon!

Discord - https://discord.gg/UB54wAv
Twitter - https://twitter.com/GameRapture
